About this application
geoOttawa is an interactive map tool that allows you to view map layers, get information and answers about the locations in the City of Ottawa. Search by address, intersections, streets, facilities, or park names to find a location. Many different map layers of information are available, such as parks, schools, City facilities, property parcels, roads, zoning, and air photos dating back to 1928. geoOttawa is your starting point for mapping available from the City of Ottawa!
Web Accessibility

However, the interactive map functionality has accessibility limitations; such as for individuals with low vision or blindness and or mobility limitations (motor disabilities) which would restrict the user from utilizing the mouse; and contains some features that may not be practical for all users. Candidate campaign finances and contributions
Campaign period

The campaign period for a candidate for Mayor, City Councillor and School Board Trustee in the 2026 Municipal Elections begins on the day they file their nomination forms with the City Clerk and ends on December 31, 2026.

Candidates cannot accept any contributions or incur any expenses after the end of the campaign period.

If at the end of the campaign period a candidate’s campaign expenses are greater than their campaign income, their campaign will be in deficit. Candidates with a deficit may extend their campaign to fundraise.

If a candidate’s campaign has a surplus, the candidate must pay the surplus to the City Clerk when filing their financial statement.

Under the Municipal Act, 2001 (the Act), municipalities have authority to appoint various statutory officers to carry out certain functions as described in the legislation. Overview

2025 Reporting
Overview

The Public Sector Salary Disclosure Act, 1996 makes Ontario’s public sector more open and accountable to taxpayers. The act requires organizations that receive public funding from the Province of Ontario to make public, by March 31 each year, the names, positions, salaries and total taxable benefits of employees paid $100,000 or more in the previous calendar year.

The act applies to organizations such as:

the Government of Ontario
Crown agencies
municipalities
hospitals
boards of public health
school boards
universities and colleges
Ontario Power Generation
other public sector employers who receive a significant level of funding from the provincial government

All employers subject to the act are required to submit their disclosure records to their funding ministries by the fifth business day of March each year using the guides and forms provided.

Operating and Capital Budget Status Reports (Q1 and Q2)

Quarterly operating and capital status reports are prepared as part of the reporting framework approved by Council. Operating reports present actual year-to-date revenues and expenditures against the amounts previously budgeted for in the corresponding period. Year-end forecasts are also presented in the second quarter report. Capital reports provide a listing of the capital projects / programs, the authorized expenditure budgets, actual expenditures and commitments incurred to date and the remaining amount to be spent. The purpose of the reports is to present either the march 31 year to date (Q1) or the June 30 year-to-date operating and capital results (Q2) for City Wide Tax Supported Programs and Rate Supported Programs along with providing a year-end forecast. To make it easier to find a decision, the Committee of Adjustment has partnered with the Canadian Legal Information Institute (CanLII) to publish decisions on their powerful digital platform, in both English and French, at no cost to the tribunal and the public.

CanLII is a non-profit organization founded by the Federation of Law Societies of Canada. Its mandate is to provide efficient and open online access to judicial and quasi-judicial decisions. It publishes Canadian court judgments and decisions from many federal and provincial administrative tribunals, including the Ontario Land Tribunal that hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions.

Ottawa’s Committee of Adjustment is the first committee of adjustment in Ontario and Canada to publish decisions on CanLII.

GTFS Real-time
GTFS Real-Time or GTFS-RT provides a standardized format for transmitting real-time updates about public transit systems. This includes information about vehicle locations, arrival times, departure times, and service alerts.
OC Transpo as part of the GTFS-RT feed provides vehicle locations and trip updates that include arrival and departure times. Service alerts is not available at this time.

GTFS Schedule
GTFS-RT is designed to work alongside the static GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) format. GTFS defines a static schedule and structure for public transit data, while GTFS-RT adds real-time updates to this data.

Download the OC Transpo GTFS static files here.

OC Transpo strongly recommends the download of GTFS Schedule file on a daily basis to ensure the GTFS-RT feed is compatible.

Update on the ASE Program in Ottawa

On October 20th, the Province of Ontario introduced Bill 56, Building a More Competitive Economy Act, 2025, which includes amendments to the Highway Traffic Act. These amendments revoke the legal authority for municipalities to operate automated speed enforcement programs in community safety zones and in school zones, while placing oversight for school zone signage under the authority of the Ministry of Transportation.

What this means for Ottawa

Come November 14, the following will take effect:

Repeal of Part XIV.1 of the Highway Traffic Act, removing the legislative authority from municipalities to issue automated speeding tickets under the automated speed enforcement program.  
This applies to all automated speed enforcement camera locations, including those in school zones.
Any tickets issued before the change will still need to be paid and continue to be processed as usual.

Drinking water
Drinking Water Quality Management System

Every day, the City of Ottawa’s central water supply provides safe drinking water to approximately 900,000 residential, commercial, and industrial customers. Using the Ottawa River as its source, drinking water is treated at two purifications plants and subsequently distributed through more than 3,000 kilometres of water main before arriving at your tap. In rural areas, the City operates six groundwater well systems.

More than 100,000 water quality tests are performed on drinking water samples annually, covering 350 parameters. The results demonstrate that City of Ottawa customers receive high-quality drinking water that meets all federal guidelines and provincial standards.

A copy of the Drinking Water Quality Management System Operation Plan is available upon request by contacting DWQMS@ottawa.ca.

geoOttawa is an interactive map tool that allows you to view map layers, get information and answers about the locations in the City of Ottawa.
